hook: Listen to a doctor on the radio and catch the fine print: what she advises, what she qualifies and which myth she corrects.
intro: An expert interview on healthy eating of about 280 words — a presenter asking, a doctor (Dr. Berg) answering — heard once. Radio and podcast interviews with experts sound like this, and the statements to mark true or false check whether you caught what was actually said. The expert’s language: advice in the imperative (Essen Sie viel Gemüse und trinken Sie genug Wasser), a qualification (Man muss übrigens nicht völlig auf Süßigkeiten verzichten; entscheidend ist das Maß), a cause (Stress und Zeitmangel führen zu schlechten Gewohnheiten), a hypothesis in the Konjunktiv (Hätten die Menschen mehr Zeit zum Kochen, würden sie ganz automatisch gesünder essen), and a rumour she corrects (Kaffee soll ja an allem schuld sein – aber die Studien sagen etwas anderes). Listen for the qualifiers — nicht völlig, meistens, eher, wenig — because false statements are usually exaggerations of what was said — just as headlines often exaggerate what an expert said — and for the subjective sollen, which reports what people say rather than what the expert thinks.
tips[0].title: The expert's moves
tips[0].text: Main advice (Mein wichtigster Rat ist …) → qualification (übrigens, nicht völlig, entscheidend ist …) → cause (… führen zu …) → hypothesis (Hätten …, würden …) → a rumour and its correction (soll ja … – aber …). Questions follow these.
tips[0].check.why: Mein wichtigster Rat ist … introduces the expert's main advice, followed by an imperative.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Advice
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Qualification
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Myth corrected
tips[1].title: Exaggeration is the classic trap
tips[1].text: 'nicht völlig verzichten' ≠ 'verzichten'. 'vor allem Gemüse' ≠ 'nur Gemüse'. A statement that drops a qualifier is false.
tips[1].check.why: nicht ganz verzichten means you don't have to give it up entirely. The other statements drop the qualifier and exaggerate.
tips[2].title: führen zu = the cause question
tips[2].text: Stress und Zeitmangel führen zu schlechten Gewohnheiten. 'Was führt zu …?' is answered by the noun before führen.
tips[2].check.why: The cause is the subject before führt zu: zu wenig Schlaf.
remember[0]: Catch the qualifiers: nicht völlig, meistens, entscheidend ist.
remember[1]: soll ja … = what people say; the expert’s own view follows after aber.
exam: Expert interviews like this are a standard listening text in the B2 exam — and on every health podcast and radio programme.
tips[0].check.q: „Mein wichtigster Rat ist: Schlafen Sie mindestens sieben Stunden.“ Which move is this?
tips[1].check.q: The expert says: „Sie müssen nicht ganz auf Fleisch verzichten.“ Which statement is true?
tips[1].check.options[0]: You can still eat some meat.
tips[1].check.options[1]: You should give up meat completely.
tips[1].check.answer: You can still eat some meat.
